SCCH-24 2 MVC 2811/2023  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 19-01-2023 at about 9.00 A.M. when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 04-HW-6857 from Rajanukunte- Yelahanka road and when he Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151599396/
1 reached near NES Bus stop, on Doddaballapura Main Road, at that time the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-0771 route No.401(K) came from NES Bus stand in the same direction and drove his vehicle towards right side without giving any indication and dashed against the motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to K.K.
Hospital wherein he took first aid treatment and then shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient and underwent Surgery.

So far the petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards treatment, Medicines, bed charges transportation, food and conveyance and incurred medical expense by obtaining loan from his relatives and friend and some bills claimed by ESI.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was working as Service Advisor at Renault Company Service Center and thereby earning sum of Rs.15, 000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner is unable to do work as earlier and cannot do daily activities.

3. The respondent/ the Managing Director, BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0771 has filed written statement and contended that on 19-01-2023 at about 9- 05 a.m., the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-0771 was proceeding from Kengeri to Yelahanka, when they came near in between Sheshadripura college bus stand and NES bus stand, at that time a motorcycle bearing No.KA- 04-HW-6857 came in a rash and negligent manner from left side of the bus and lost balance over his vehicle and came in contact with the left rear portion of the bus and fell down.
The driver of the motorcycle has no experience to drive the vehicle on main roads and the petitioner was not having valid and effective driving licence.
It is further contended that if the rider of motorcycle had taken little bit precautionary at the time of riding the vehicle, the said accident could have been avoided.
It is further contended that petitioner himself is responsible for the accident but not the driver of BMTC bus.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the RTA alleged to have occurred on 19-01-2023 at about 9.00 A.M., near NES bus stand,
Doddaballapura main Road, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, due to rash ad negligent driving of the driver of BMTC bus bearing No.KA- 57-F-0771?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and three witnesses as P.W.2 to 4 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P25 and closed evidence on his side.

On the other hand, the driver of BMTC bus by name Sri Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151599396/
2

sentences.text: Sudarshan Babu is examined as RW.1.
During the cross-examination of PW.1 the learned counsel for respondent has confronted the true copy of discharge summary and got marked Ex.R1.

6. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.
, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 19-01-2023 at about 9.00 A.M. when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.

No.KA-04-HW-6857 from Rajanukunte - Yelahanka road and when he reached near NES Bus stop,
on Doddaballapura Main Road, at that time the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-0771 (hereinafter dreferred to as offending vehicle) route No.401(K) came from NES Bus stand in the same direction and drove his vehicle towards right side without showing any indication and dashed against the motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
9.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Mahazar, sketch, Wound certificate, IMV reports, Charge sheet, 133 notice and 133 notice reply are the material documents to prove the present issue.
10.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri Goutham Gunaal S.G., case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.46/2023 of Yelahanka Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.134 (a&b) R/W 187 of IMV Act.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section under section 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.134 (a&b) R/W 187 of IMV Act.

11. It is categorically contended both in the written statement and in the evidence of Rw1 that at the time of accident the driver of BMTC bus was driving the bus in careful manner and correct side of the road by sounding the horn; hence he is no way responsible for the accident.

12. The learned counsel for respondent during the course of argument has much stated about the delay of 20 days in lodging the complaint and by referring Ex.R1 i.e., the discharge summary issued from Ramaiah Hospital has submitted that the petitioner has sustained injury due to skid and fall.

3 13.

entities.text: Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the contention taken by the respondent, if the evidence placed on record is perused, it is true that the accident in question has occurred on 19- 01-2023 and complaint came to be lodged on 07-02-2023 and there is delay of nearly 19 days in lodging the complaint.
In the complaint and FIR the reason for delay in lodging the complaint is satisfactory explained stating that it is after the petitioner regained conscious, he lodged the complaint.
If the Ex.P1 is perused, it is given by the complainant himself.

As per the discharge summary issued from Ramaiah Hospital,
the petitioner has taken treatment at the first instance from 19-01-2023 to 07-03- 2023.
It means for nearly 49 days the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient.
Though complaint is lodged at belated stage but soon after the accident the petitioner has taken treatment at Life Care Hospital.
In the certificate as per Ex.P7 given by the Life Care Unity Hospital, the history of injury is mentioned as "hit by BMTC Bus".
As per the Ex.P11 and Ex.P12 ie., IP bill of Life Care Unity Hospital, the petitioner has taken primary treatment in the said hospital and incurred medical expenses Rs.21,200/-.
It means, in the hospital where the petitioner has taken primary treatment, the history of injury is given as "hit by BMTC bus".
Further except Ex.R1 in all the medical records the history of injury is mentioned as "RTA hit by BMTC bus".
Even in the Ex.R1 the history of injury is mentioned as "RTA" followed by the word skid and fall.

If the written statement of respondent and evidence in chief of Rw.1 is perused, nowhere they have they disputed the accidental injuries sustained by the petitioner and nowhere they have taken the contention that the petitioner has sustained injury due to "skid and fall".

Hence, when petitioner has taken treatment immediately after the accident under the history of RTA, under such circumstances the mere fact that there is delay in lodging the complaint that would not go to the route of the case of the petitioner.

14. Coming to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the respondent is concerned, it is not in dispute that petitioner and offending vehicle was proceeding on the same direction in Rajankunte -Yelahanka road.
If spot mahazar and sketch is perused, it is a double road of the width of 20 x 20 feet.
The accident in question has occurred at a distance of nearly 12 feet from the left edge of tar road leads to Rajankunte -Yelahanka.

It is not in dispute that offending vehicle was proceeding on the left side of said road and petitioner was preceding parallel to the offending vehicle on its right side in between offending vehicle and divider.

15. The learned counsel for respondent by referring the aforesaid evidence has vehemently submitted that since petitioner was proceeding in the two wheeler which is a light vehicle he ought to have ride his vehicle on the left side of road instead on right side.

16. So far as the said contention taken by the respondent is concerned, when it is a double road and both petitioner and respondent are plying in one way road and when the offending vehicle was proceeding on the left side of road parallel to the vehicle of the petitioner under such circumstances it is quite natural for the petitioner to ride his vehicle on the right side of the road.
As it is one way road, if the road is free on the right side of the road, there is nothing wrong in petitioner riding his vehicle on the right side of the road.

If the sketch is perused, the offending vehicle which was proceeding on the left side of the road when it reached the spot of accident took the vehicle towards right side and hit against the vehicle of the petitioner which was proceeding on the right side of the said road.
If the offending vehicle had not come towards right side from the left side this accident would not have occurred.

Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151599396/
4 17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though by referring Ex.R1 the respondent has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident but in the written statement the respondent has taken the contention that the petitioner by riding his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner from left side of the bus, lost balance and contacted left rear portion of the bus and fell down.
Even in the evidence of RW.1 he has deposed to the same effect.

The respondent having taken contention in the written statement and in their evidence that the petitioner was riding his vehicle on the left side of the road and that his vehicle came in contact with the left rear portion of the bus, but during the cross examination of PW.1 the respondent has taken all together different contention by stating that the left handle of the vehicle of petitioner rubbed on the right rear portion of the bus.
Hence, it can be said that the respondent is not definite as to the manner in which accident in question has occurred.
From time to time the respondent changes his version regarding the manner in which accident in question has occurred.
If really accident is caused due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner then nothing prevented the respondent from lodging the complaint.
Admittedly, the driver of the offending vehicle has not lodged the complaint.
Further though charge sheet is filed against the driver but they have not challenged the charge sheet.
Hence, from the materials placed on record it can be said that the rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for accident.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summaries which are marked at Ex.P.4 and Ex.P11.

On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at M.S. Ramaiah Hospital for two times from 19-01-2023 to 07-03-2023 and from 19- 07-2023 to 20-07-2023 in all for a period of 47 days.
As per wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained six injuries which are grievous in nature.
19. Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopedic surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospitals, Bengaluru, is examined as PW4 and through him, out patient record and X-ray are got marked as Ex.P.24 and 25.
PW.4 deposed that he examined the petitioner clinically, radiologically for assessment of disability.

PW.4 further deposed that petitioner has suffered disability of pelvis and both lower limbs at 35%
and whole body physical disability at 17%.
PW.4 further deposed that petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up.
20. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
21. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained grievous injuries and simple injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
22. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, he has produced medical bill for Rs.87,249/- .
As such petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.87,249/- under the head medical expenses.

Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151599396/
5 23.

entities.text: Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that petitioner was aged about 26 years and he was working as Service Advisor at Renault Company Service Center and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
The petitioner has produced bank statement as per Ex.P.15.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- p.m.
24.

The petitioner has sustained grievous injury and taken treatment for 47 days as inpatient in M.S.
Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of four months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15,000/- p.m. for four months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period .
25. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 47 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
The petitioner has produced ambulance bill for Rs.2,500/-.
As petitioner has sustained grievous injuries there is every possibility of his hiring ambulance to shift from spot of accident to K.K Hospital.
Hence, ambulance bill for Rs.2,500/- is to be taken into consideration.
26. The petitioner has produced receipt three in number issued by Apoorva Home Nursing Service for Rs.23,000/-, Rs..16,080/- and Rs.35,360/-.
As per the evidence of Pw.1 he has engaged the service of Home nurse to look after him while he was taking treatment in the hospital and even after discharge from the hospital.
As observed supra, petitioner has taken treatment in all for a period of 47 days.
Hence, the possibility of home nurse engaged by petitioner cannot be ruled out.
Hence, this court inclines to take the attendants charges for two months at the rate of Rs.18,000/- per month.
If the medical records are perused, the petitioner has taken treatment for number of times as outpatient.
Hence taking into consideration the expenses incurred by the petitioner for transportation, attendants charges and other incidental charges, he is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/-.
27. The PW.4 has assessed the permanent disability of petitioner on both lower limbs and Pelvis at 35% and whole body physical disability at 17%.

Taking in to consideration the evidence of PW.4 given in his cross examination this court finds it just to assess the disability at14% instead of 17%.
28.
It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 26 years.

In this regard, the petitioner has produced DL and Aadhaar card of the petitioner which show his date of birth as 06-05- 1996 and as the accident in question took place in the year 2023, it can be said that deceased was aged about 27 years as on the date of accident.
29.

So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,000/- p.m and if 14% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 27 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 is '17'.

So by applying the multiplier '17' the future loss of Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151599396/
6 income due to disability comes to Rs.4,28,400/- (i.e.,Rs.15,500 x 14% x 17 x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,28,400/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
30. As per the evidence of Pw4, the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant the estimate cost of the surgery is Rs.40,000/-.
But admittedly PW.4 has not given estimation.
Hence, this court inclines to award future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.20,000/-.
31. The petitioner at his age of 27 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of comfort and amenities Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.N Heads Amount o.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 75,000/-

2 . Towards transportation, attendants Rs. 60,000/-
 charges and other incidental  charges

3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 60,000/-
 laid up period 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 87,249/-
5. Loss of future income Rs.4,28,400/-

6 . Future Medical expenses Rs. 20,000/-
7. Discomfort and amenities Rs. 50,000/-
Total Rs 7,80,649/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.7,80,649/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Eighty Thousand Six Hundred Forty Nine only)
32.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent this court directs the respondent to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
33. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,80,649/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Eighty Thousand Six Hundred Forty Nine only) with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its Pritham Prahalad S.G vs B.M.T.C on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151599396/
7 realization.
The Respondent is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 1st day of October 2024.)
